title: Fix long-context regression: adjust prefill regime thresholds to avoid tail-latency spikes
text:
description:
Context: During perf characterization + Hosted canary for runtime 1.21, we saw a p99 regression on long-context workloads (>=16k prompt tokens) on L40S and some A100 pools when kernel auto-selection v2 classified certain requests into the “mid” prefill bucket and chose FA3 prefill variants that are great for short/mid contexts but showed allocator/workspace churn at long context (and worse tail when batch composition is mixed). This PR tightens the v2 rules to prevent mis-selection in the long-context regime while keeping determinism guarantees and preserving the gains on short/mid prompts. Changes: (1) Adjust prefill-length bucket boundaries and add a small hysteresis band to reduce flip-flopping around thresholds when scheduler-provided distribution hints are noisy. (2) Add an explicit long-context guard: for ctx >= LONG_CTX_TOKENS (default 12288), prefer the “lc_prefill” kernels when available, otherwise fall back to the known-stable v1-equivalent prefill path. (3) Add SKU-aware exception for L40S where the problematic kernel variant was disproportionately impacting tail; we now require a stricter threshold before selecting it and we prefer the stable alternative when decode_len is small (prefill-dominant requests). (4) Add unit tests covering boundary conditions + replay determinism around bucket edges, including cases with mixed scheduler hints. Bench results: See attached before/after plots from perf suite run 2026-02-14 and canary replay slice. Summary on L40S (long-context summarization profile, 16k/256): p95 1.38s -> 1.11s (-19.6%), p99 2.74s -> 1.63s (-40.5%). On A100 (same profile): p95 1.02s -> 0.98s (-3.9%), p99 1.88s -> 1.61s (-14.4%). No correctness diffs observed (golden outputs match within expected nondeterminism bounds; selection remains deterministic for fixed inputs). Notes: This is intended as a targeted rule tweak; no changes to telemetry schema. Rollout: safe to land in release/1.21 behind existing gates; recommended to promote to Hosted canary first, then Dedicated pools after 24h with the rollout dashboard guardrails. Artifacts/plots: Before/after plot bundle: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/plots/index.html ; Comparison table: gs://redwood-perf-artifacts/kernel-select-v2/28522-longctx-prefill-thresholds/summary.csv . Checklist: [x] Adds/updates unit tests for bucket boundaries and long-context guard [x] Verifies selector determinism tests still pass [x] Runs perf suite subset (Llama/Mistral long-context + mixed) on A100 + L40S [x] Confirms no telemetry cardinality changes [x] Updates release/1.21 notes comment (see thread) to mention long-context fix (internal) [x] Linked SUP-31842 for traceability

review_conversation:
Hiro Tanaka (review): The guard looks right, but I’m worried about thrash around the boundary when scheduler hints are “mostly long” but a single request is 8–10k. Can we ensure we don’t oscillate between kernels within the same warm pool? Also please justify the 12288 default. Yuki Sato (author): Added hysteresis band using a two-threshold approach when distribution_hint is present (enter long_ctx at 12k, exit at 10k) to reduce oscillation. Default 12288 matches the prefill workspace knee we saw in perf plots across L40S and A100; linked plot bundle in description. Lena Fischer (review): For mixed workloads, can you include decode_len in the guard? Some of the worst spikes were prefill-dominant. Yuki Sato: Updated rule ordering so the long_ctx guard checks (ctx_tokens >= 12288 && decode_tokens <= 512) before the generic bucket-based choice, which matches the spike signature. Omar El-Sayed (review): Please confirm we’re not changing telemetry cardinality; last week’s incident thread was noisy. Also add a log-only counter for how often this guard triggers so we can validate during rollout. Yuki Sato: No schema changes. Added a single aggregated counter kernel_select_v2.long_ctx_guard_triggered (no extra tags beyond existing model_family/gpu_sku/region sampling policy). Marcus Reed (review): Bench numbers look good, but I’d like to see at least one run on Qwen long-context profile as well. Yuki Sato: Added Qwen2.5-14B long-context run results to the same artifact bundle; deltas are neutral-to-positive (p99 -9% on L40S). Allison Grant (review): Can we add a short note to release/1.21 internal notes so oncall knows this is the fix for SUP-31842? Yuki Sato: Added a brief entry under “Kernel selection v2” in the internal known-issues/release notes file. Approvals: Hiro (approved), Lena (approved), Omar (approved), Marcus (approved).

release_notes:
Internal: Kernel auto-selection v2 adjusts long-context prefill thresholds/guard to prevent tail-latency spikes on long-context, prefill-dominant workloads (notably L40S). No user-facing config changes; controlled via existing feature gate.

title: Add TP long-context stress scenarios + thresholds (A100/H100) and wire into CI gating
text:
body:
Context: As part of ENG-4821/ENG-4828 (TP stability fixes), we need a repeatable long-context workload in perf-canary that exercises the failure modes we’ve seen under sustained mixed prefill/decode. Current TP coverage mostly targets short/medium contexts and does not reliably surface the “prefill spike -> decode starvation -> collective stall” class of issues.

What this PR does:
- Adds two new TP stress scenarios focused on long-context prefill + sustained decode:
  - tp_longctx_a100_80gb_tp4: long-context (32k) prefill, streaming decode, concurrency ramp
  - tp_longctx_h100_tp8: long-context (64k) prefill, streaming decode, higher steady-state concurrency
- Defines pass/fail thresholds that are explicitly stability-first (hang/timeout detection) and perf-aware (p50/p99 and throughput deltas vs baseline).
- Wires the scenarios into CI (GitHub Actions) as a gated workflow for PRs that opt-in via label (ci/gate-perf) and as a nightly on main for drift detection.
- Adds documentation on scenario intent, runtime flags, and how to interpret failures.

Scenario details (high level):
- Workload shape:
  - Prompts: weighted distribution with a heavy long-context bucket (>= 28k tokens) plus a smaller short bucket to keep scheduling pressure realistic.
  - Decode: streaming on, 256–512 tokens per request, mixed stop reasons.
  - Concurrency: ramp 1 -> 8 (A100) and 2 -> 16 (H100) with a steady-state hold to catch slow stalls.
  - Duration: ~12–15 min per scenario (kept under our runner window).
- Stability thresholds:
  - No run-level hang: scenario must complete within max_wall_clock (hard cap).
  - No “silent stall”: fails if progress heartbeat is absent for > 30s (client-side) OR if step-level throughput drops below min_tokens_per_sec for > 90s.
  - Request timeout rate <= 0.1% (timeouts are treated as hard failures unless explicitly annotated as infra).
- Perf thresholds:
  - Throughput regression > 5% vs baseline on the same runner type fails.
  - p99 end-to-end latency regression > 10% vs baseline fails.

CI/Gating:
- New workflow: tp-longctx-stress.yml
  - Runs on pull_request if label ci/gate-perf is present (keeps PR loop fast by default).
  - Runs nightly on main for both A100 and H100 runner pools.
- Artifacts:
  - Uploads run summary JSON + CSV timeseries (tokens/sec, p50/p99 latency, timeout counters) and the rendered report.
  - Includes runner metadata (GPU type, driver, NCCL, CUDA) to simplify correlations during triage.

Why label-gated instead of always-on:
- These are intentionally heavier than our smoke perf runs and require GPU runners. The label approach lets runtime PRs opt-in when touching TP scheduling/kernels while still giving us nightly signal for drift.

How to run locally (dev):
- ./bin/canary run scenarios/tp/tp_longctx_a100_80gb_tp4.yaml --set runtime.tp.enabled=true
- ./bin/canary report --input out/latest --format html

Docs:
- Adds a new section under docs/scenarios/tensor-parallel.md describing the long-context workloads, thresholds, and common failure patterns (scheduler starvation vs comms stall vs infra runner issues).

Notes / follow-ups:
- We intentionally kept the thresholds conservative to catch stalls/hangs first. Once ENG-4824/4825 land broadly, we can tighten perf budgets and add a mixed prefill/decode cancellation subtest.

Checklist:
- [x] Scenario configs added + validated on bench-lab A100/H100
- [x] Thresholds tuned against 3 baseline runs
- [x] CI workflow added + artifact upload verified
- [x] Docs updated

References:
- ENG-4828 (perf-canary TP stress scenarios)
- ENG-4821 (initiative umbrella)
- Related runtime work: tp watchdog + heartbeat metrics (see redwood PRs in ENG-4823/4826)

conversation:
Marcus Reed (review): The stability thresholds look good, but I’m worried about false positives from transient runner hiccups. Can we distinguish “no progress” from “low throughput” and add a short grace window after ramp changes?
Rina Kobayashi (author): Yep. I split the detector into (a) heartbeat absence (hard fail after 30s) and (b) sustained low throughput (fail after 90s). I also added a 20s grace period after each concurrency step to avoid tripping while the system re-stabilizes. Pushed in 8c1a2f4.
Kira Volkov (review): Baseline comparison: are we pinning by runner type + CUDA/NCCL versions? Otherwise baseline drift will be noisy.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Baselines are keyed on (scenario_id, runner_pool, gpu_name, driver, cuda, nccl). Nightly updates the baseline only on green runs. Added that metadata to the artifact summary as well. See commit 2f9b7d1.
Aisha Bello (review): For alertability later, can we ensure the summary includes timeout_rate and a single “stall_reason” field when failing? Helps with dashboards if we mirror this logic.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added timeout_rate to the top-level summary and introduced stall_reason enum: HEARTBEAT_GAP / LOW_TOKENS_PER_SEC / MAX_WALL_CLOCK / PERF_REGRESSION. See 41d0c6a.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI wiring: label-gated is fine, but please ensure the workflow is not required for all PRs. Also double check secrets usage on fork PRs.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Confirmed: workflow only runs on pull_request when label ci/gate-perf exists and uses internal self-hosted runners + repo-scoped secrets, so it won’t execute on forks. Updated docs/ci/perf-gating.md to spell this out.
Marcus Reed (approval): Ran on bench-lab (A100) and it caught the expected long-prefill throughput dip without failing. CI green. LGTM.

title: Long-context prefill stress workload (summarization-style) w/ KV cache pressure + prefill latency metrics
text:
Context
We need a representative workload for long-context summarization and similar “large prefill, modest decode” shapes. This cohort is a major driver of p99 TTFT in production and is sensitive to scheduler backpressure, KV cache settings, and kernel selection around long sequence lengths.

This ticket defines + implements the long-context prefill stress workload in the benchmark harness, including (a) realistic sequence length distributions derived from prod telemetry cohorts (without prompt content), (b) explicit measurement of prefill latency / TTFT, and (c) controlled KV cache pressure scenarios to surface regressions in cache mgmt and scheduling.

Goals
- Add a workload generator mode: long_context_prefill_v1 (summarization-style).
- Exercise prefill-heavy behavior:
  - Large input lengths (prefill) with relatively small output lengths (decode).
  - Concurrency sufficient to trigger continuous batching + queueing.
- Produce stable, reproducible metrics for baseline sweeps:
  - TTFT p50/p95/p99 (streaming and non-streaming variants).
  - Prefill latency breakdown (server-side prefill time where available; otherwise TTFT boundary as per ADR-0172).
  - TPOT p50/p95/p99 for modest decode.
  - Throughput tokens/s (prefill tokens/s + decode tokens/s where reported).
- Surface KV cache pressure behavior:
  - Cold vs warm KV/prefix cache reporting.
  - Controlled cache residency pressure (cache thrash scenario) to reveal cliffs.
- Integrate with run manifest schema (ADR-0172) and produce artifacts for dashboards.

Non-goals
- New model onboarding beyond what’s required to run top models already in the baseline matrix.
- “Best possible” marketing benchmarks. This is internal representativeness + regression detection first.

Workload definition (v1)
Name
- workload_id: long_context_prefill_v1

Request shape
- Mode A (baseline): summarization_prefill_heavy
  - Input length bins (tokens): 4k / 8k / 16k / 32k (distribution below)
  - Output length bins (tokens): 128 / 256 / 512 (mostly 256)
  - Sampling: deterministic params for perf stability (temperature=0, top_p=1). If model requires temperature>0 for correctness, pin to a fixed value and record in manifest.

Sequence length distribution (initial; calibrated from telemetry cohorts)
- 4k: 20%
- 8k: 35%
- 16k: 35%
- 32k: 10%
Notes:
- Keep a hard cap at model_context_window - safety_margin (e.g., -256 tokens) to avoid variable truncation behavior.
- Store the distribution and bins explicitly in the run manifest.

Concurrency / arrival model
- Concurrency target: 8, 16, 32 (sweepable; baseline uses 16 unless otherwise specified)
- Arrival: closed-loop with think-time=0 for saturation, plus an optional open-loop mode for stability checks.
- Warmup: required (see Variance control).

Caching scenarios (must report both)
- Cold scenario:
  - Disable prefix cache for the workload OR ensure unique prompts per request so caches do not hit.
  - Report as cache_mode=cold.
- Warm scenario:
  - Fixed prompt set with high overlap (e.g., same long prefix with small suffix variance) to trigger prefix/KV reuse where supported.
  - Report as cache_mode=warm.
- Thrash scenario (optional, nightly only):
  - Over-subscribe KV cache budget by rotating prompt set beyond cache capacity; intended to expose eviction/regression behavior.

Measurement boundaries / metrics
- Canonical metrics per ADR-0172 (reference): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0172-benchmark-metrics-and-run-manifest-format.json
- TTFT definition for this workload:
  - Streaming: server-side “first token on wire” timestamp when available; otherwise client-observed first byte with client overhead flagged.
  - Non-streaming: TTFT recorded as time-to-complete-first-response (still useful but not preferred).
- Prefill latency:
  - If runtime exports server-side prefill_ms, record it.
  - If not available, approximate with TTFT (explicitly labeled as prefill_proxy=ttft).
- KV cache pressure signals:
  - Record configured KV cache limits/knobs in manifest (bytes, pages, eviction policy if applicable).
  - Capture cache hit rate and eviction counters if emitted by runtime instrumentation; otherwise record “not_available”.

Variance control (required)
- Standard warmup procedure before measurement window:
  - 2 minutes warmup OR N requests per concurrency level (whichever is longer).
  - Discard warmup samples from reported percentiles.
- GPU determinism recommendations:
  - Lock clocks where permitted in benchmark fleet; record in env capture.
  - Pin container placement / isolate noisy neighbors per SRE guidance.
- Sample size:
  - Minimum 200 completed requests per (model, region, sku, cache_mode, concurrency) cell for percentiles.

Acceptance criteria
- Workload generator merged in benchmark-lab with:
  - CLI/config support to select long_context_prefill_v1.
  - Deterministic seed control.
  - Output exports include TTFT/TPOT percentiles and throughput.
  - Run manifest includes: sequence length bins + distribution, output bins, cache_mode, concurrency, warmup policy.
- Validated representativeness:
  - Applied ML/Evals sign-off that bins + distribution reflect production cohort shapes (no sensitive prompt content).
- Reproducibility:
  - Two back-to-back runs on same cell show <5% drift on p50 TTFT and <10% drift on p99 TTFT after warmup (unless flagged by SRE as fleet instability).
- Dashboard readiness:
  - Results include tags required by perf baseline dashboards spec.

Implementation plan
1) Define workload config (Claire + Rina)
- Finalize bins/distributions + concurrency defaults.
- Ensure it maps to “long-context summarization” cohort in telemetry (ADR-0173).

2) Implement generator + harness wiring (Marcus)
- Add workload implementation under benchmark-lab workloads/
- Add warmup + sample discard logic.
- Add cache_mode flags and prompt set generation logic.

3) Instrumentation / manifest fields (Logan + Omar)
- Ensure env/run manifest captures:
  - KV cache config
  - scheduler policy snapshot
  - kernel selection summary (if available)
- If runtime supports prefill timing, wire export; else mark prefill_proxy.

4) Validation run + calibration (Sana + Sean)
- Run on a single stable cell (us-east, H100) to establish variance profile.
- Adjust warmup/sample sizes if needed.

Links / references
- Plan: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/q1-2026-perf-baseline-plan.json
- Representative suite definition: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/representative-workload-suite-v1.json
- Scheduler baseline: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/scheduler-policy-baseline-q1-2026.json
- Kernel selection matrix: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-selection-matrix-q1-2026.json
- Profiling playbook: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/perf-suite-profiling-playbook.json
- Related PR: sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-21471-add-long-context-prefill-workload-and-warmup.json

Notes / open questions
- Do we require streaming mode for this workload in gating? Current proposal: nightly runs include streaming; PR gating uses non-streaming unless a streaming-specific change is under test.
- KV cache “warm” semantics vary by deployment (prefix cache vs KV reuse). For now, treat warm scenario as “best effort cache reuse” and require explicit tagging.

Updates
- 2025-11-26 (Rina): Draft bins/distribution proposed; waiting on Applied ML confirmation against telemetry cohorts.
- 2025-12-03 (Jonas): Confirmed this is a top-3 variance driver for runtime releases; please ensure manifest includes cache_mode and concurrency.
- 2025-12-12 (Sean): Benchmark fleet stability note: lock clocks where possible; enforce warmup; isolate nodes. Suggest making thrash scenario nightly-only.
- 2026-01-07 (Marcus): Implemented generator scaffolding + warmup discard; adding cache_mode plumbing next.
- 2026-01-22 (Claire): Methodology note: TTFT boundary must match ADR-0172; if client-observed, label client_overhead=true and include RTT stats.
- 2026-02-04 (Marcus): Merged benchmark-lab PR-21471. Long-context workload now in harness; includes warmup + export. Remaining: add “thrash” preset (optional) + verify cache hit metrics on runtime build.
- 2026-02-18 (Rina): Validation complete on us-east/H100 with two-run drift within target after warmup. Marking Done; follow-ups captured in ENG-4826 for additional scheduler counters + in perf-canary threshold tuning ticket.

title: Kernel auto-selection v2 — Known issues and workarounds
text:
## Purpose
This page is the living source of truth for *known issues* in Kernel auto-selection v2 ("KASv2") and the approved workarounds (denylist/allowlist rules, overrides, guardrails).

**Audience:** Runtime oncall, SRE, Release Engineering, Dedicated/Private customer readiness.

**Scope:** Issues that can impact correctness, determinism/replayability, p95/p99 latency, throughput stability, or operational clarity during rollout.

---

## Quick triage checklist (oncall)
1) **Confirm it is KASv2-related**
   - Check dashboard panel: selection distribution + latency delta (v1 vs v2) for the affected model/GPU/region.
   - Verify request traces include selector fields (`selector_version=2`, chosen kernel, seq bucket).

2) **If tail latency spike or correctness concern**
   - Apply the safest mitigation first:
     - Disable v2 for *model+region* (preferred) or *GPU SKU* if localized.
     - Pin kernel to stable fallback if disabling v2 is too broad.
   - Validate recovery using p95/p99 and error rate within 10–20 minutes.

3) **Capture minimum artifacts**
   - Selection trace sample (10–50 requests): features, candidates, chosen kernel.
   - GPU SKU normalization string(s), driver/CUDA versions, model id + revision.
   - Workload description: prompt length distribution + decode lengths (or observed bucket).

For exact commands and config locations, use: **Kernel selection v2 override and rollback runbook**.

---

## Known issues index
| ID | Severity | Symptom | Affected | Status | Recommended mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| KASV2-001 | High | p99 regression on long-context prefill | Llama-family long-context (>16k) on mixed fleets | Mitigated via rule tweak; watchlist | Disable v2 for model in region; or force prefill kernel fallback |
| KASV2-002 | High | Kernel crash / CUDA illegal memory access | L40S + driver 535.x + FlashAttn v3 path | Active (denylisted) | Denylist kernel on SKU+driver; pin to FA2 fallback |
| KASV2-003 | Medium | Throughput jitter on mixed workloads | H100 pools with rapidly shifting seq regime | Active (needs tuning) | Enable scheduler seq-distribution hints; increase decision cache TTL |
| KASV2-004 | Medium | Non-deterministic selection across replicas | MIG partitions / inconsistent SKU strings | Active (guardrail) | Normalize SKU; disable v2 when `gpu_partitioned=true` until normalized |
| KASV2-005 | Medium | FP8 decode instability / quality drift | H100 FP8 decode kernels on specific model variants | Active (allowlist-only) | Keep kernels allowlisted per model revision; fall back to BF16 |
| KASV2-006 | Low | Telemetry cardinality / dashboard noise | High model+kernel combinations during canary | Mitigated | Reduce sampling; aggregate candidate set; update queries |

---

## Detailed issues

### KASV2-001 — Long-context prefill mis-selection causing tail latency spikes
**Severity:** High (SLO risk)

**Symptom**
- p95 stable but **p99 spikes** (often +25–80%) for long-context workloads.
- Spikes correlate with requests where prefill tokens exceed the selector’s long-context threshold.

**Affected**
- Model families: Llama variants (including instruct), some Qwen long-context fine-tunes.
- Workload: prefill >16k tokens, or mixed traffic where the long-context share is low but impactful.
- Fleets: more pronounced on heterogeneous fleets (A100 + L40S) due to differing kernel sweet spots.

**Likely cause**
- Seq-length regime bucketing for prefill was too permissive in mixed workloads; selector chose a kernel optimized for mid-length prefill which has worse tail behavior at >16k.

**Detection signals**
- Selector telemetry shows `seq_bucket=prefill_mid` or `prefill_decode=mixed` even when observed prefill tokens are in the long bucket.
- Latency delta panel spikes only for `seq_bucket` transitions.

**Workarounds (approved)**
1) **Disable v2 for the affected model in the affected region** (preferred for immediate stabilization).
2) **Force/pin prefill kernel** for the model on the affected SKU(s) if disabling v2 is too broad.
3) **Temporary allowlist restriction**: only enable v2 for that model on GPU SKUs where long-context kernel has been validated.

**Notes / follow-ups**
- This is partially addressed by threshold updates shipped during Runtime 1.21 canary tuning. Still a watchlist item due to workload diversity.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-21

---

### KASV2-002 — L40S + driver 535.x crash on FlashAttention v3 kernel path
**Severity:** High (correctness + availability)

**Symptom**
- Occasional worker crash with:
  - `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`
  - or `misaligned address` originating from attention kernel launch.

**Affected**
- GPU SKU: L40S (not consistently reproducible on A100/H100)
- Driver/CUDA: NVIDIA 535.x (most reports on 535.129–535.161)
- Kernel family: FlashAttention v3 attention kernels (prefill + decode variants)

**Likely cause**
- Driver interaction with FA3 kernel variant under specific head dimensions / rotary embedding settings.

**Workarounds (approved)**
- **Hard denylist** the FA3 kernel variants for `gpu_sku=L40S` when `driver_major=535`.
- Fallback to FA2 or baseline attention kernels per ADR fallback precedence.
- If Dedicated/Private cannot change drivers quickly: keep denylist and plan driver upgrade.

**Operational guidance**
- If crash rate > 0.1% of requests on the pool, treat as rollback trigger for v2 on that pool.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-25

---

### KASV2-003 — Throughput jitter on H100 pools under mixed seq regimes
**Severity:** Medium (performance stability)

**Symptom**
- Throughput oscillates (e.g., ±10–20%) across 5–15 minute windows.
- p95 latency may remain acceptable; p99 can degrade during oscillation.

**Affected**
- GPU SKU: H100 (SXM and PCIe), especially when pools run both short chat and long summarization.
- Workload: time-varying traffic mix (diurnal) or bursty long-context jobs.

**Likely cause**
- Selector decisions are correct per-request, but too reactive without using recent workload distribution hints; frequent switching between kernels interacts poorly with batching/kv-cache locality.

**Workarounds (approved)**
1) **Enable scheduler seq-distribution hints** to the selector (requires control-plane config + runtime flag in the pool).
2) Increase decision cache reuse for `(model_revision, gpu_sku, seq_bucket)` when the fleet is stable.
3) If jitter persists, restrict v2 to stable kernels only (allowlist) for that model family on H100.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-18

---

### KASV2-004 — Non-deterministic selection due to inconsistent GPU SKU normalization (incl. MIG)
**Severity:** Medium (determinism + operability)

**Symptom**
- Same request (features identical) yields different chosen kernel across replicas.
- Replay tests pass in CI but fail intermittently in specific clusters.

**Affected**
- Environments where GPU identity strings differ by:
  - cloud instance naming
  - driver reporting differences
  - MIG partition naming (e.g., `A100 40GB MIG 1g.5gb`)

**Likely cause**
- Selector key includes normalized `gpu_sku`. If normalization differs across nodes, candidate sets differ.

**Workarounds (approved)**
- Apply the SKU normalization patch set in the fleet (control-plane normalization + runtime canonicalization).
- Until normalization is confirmed, **disable v2 when `gpu_partitioned=true`** (MIG) for production pools.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-12

---

### KASV2-005 — FP8 decode instability / quality drift on H100 for specific model variants
**Severity:** Medium (quality + stability)

**Symptom**
- No crash, but:
  - increased token-level mismatch vs baseline
  - occasional decode instability (retries / early termination)
  - customer-reported “weird outputs” localized to a model revision

**Affected**
- GPU SKU: H100
- Kernel: FP8 decode kernels (variant-specific)
- Models: certain fine-tunes where activation ranges differ from base checkpoints

**Likely cause**
- FP8 kernel path requires stricter calibration assumptions than BF16; some model revisions violate expected ranges.

**Workarounds (approved)**
- Keep FP8 decode **allowlist-only**:
  - allowlist by `(model_revision, gpu_sku)`
  - default fallback to BF16 decode when not explicitly allowed
- For Dedicated/Private: provide an explicit config knob to disable FP8 decode kernels while keeping v2 enabled.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-23

---

### KASV2-006 — Telemetry cardinality increase causing dashboard noise / false alerts
**Severity:** Low (observability)

**Symptom**
- Alert fatigue: perf-canary / rollout panels show scattered spikes.
- Metrics backend reports high cardinality due to `candidate_kernels` / `kernel_variant` tags.

**Affected**
- Canary regions with high model diversity.

**Workarounds (approved)**
- Reduce sampling rate for verbose selector events.
- Emit candidate set as a **hashed bucket** instead of raw list.
- Update dashboards to group by `kernel_family` rather than `kernel_variant` where possible.

**Last verified**: 2026-02-14

---

## Temporary allowlist/denylist rules (current)
**Important:** Treat these as time-bound. Each rule must have an owner and an expiry/review date.

| Rule | Type | Scope | Rationale | Owner | Review by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Disable v2 on L40S + driver 535.x | Deny | gpu_sku + driver | Avoid FA3 crash path (KASV2-002) | Isabella Rossi | 2026-03-08 |
| Disable v2 for `llama-3.1-70b` in `us-east1` | Deny | model + region | Long-context p99 regression observed in canary (KASV2-001) | Yuki Sato | 2026-03-01 |
| FP8 decode kernels on H100 | Allow | gpu_sku + model_revision | Prevent quality drift for unvalidated fine-tunes (KASV2-005) | Noah Patel | 2026-03-15 |
| Disable v2 when `gpu_partitioned=true` | Deny | pool attribute | Determinism risk until SKU normalization complete (KASV2-004) | Jordan Lee | 2026-03-05 |

### Example policy snippet (illustrative)
Use the control-plane policy engine configuration format from the rollout runbook. Example below demonstrates the intent only.

- Deny v2 on L40S with driver 535.x:
  - match: gpu_sku == "L40S" AND nvidia_driver_major == 535
  - action: set selector_version = 1

- Allow FP8 decode kernels only for validated model revisions:
  - match: gpu_sku IN {"H100-SXM", "H100-PCIe"} AND model_revision IN {"qwen2.5-72b@2026-02-10", "llama-3.1-8b@2026-02-01"}
  - action: allow kernel_family = "decode_fp8"
  - else: force kernel_family = "decode_bf16"

---

## Customer-facing guidance (Dedicated/Private)
- If the customer has a constrained SKU (single GPU type), prefer **pinning a known-stable kernel** over frequent policy changes.
- For driver-sensitive issues (e.g., L40S 535.x), recommend a driver upgrade plan; use denylist as interim safety.
- Always document any override in the customer’s deployment record and include:
  - model(s), region(s), sku(s)
  - start time + expected duration
  - success criteria + rollback criteria

---

## How to add a new known issue
When adding an item, include:
- Unique ID (`KASV2-###`)
- Severity (High/Medium/Low) and impact area (correctness/perf/determinism/ops)
- Repro info: model revision, GPU SKU, driver/CUDA, seq bucket/workload
- Detection signals: metrics + telemetry fields
- Workaround: exact deny/allow/override guidance and blast radius
- Owner + review-by date

**Escalation:** If correctness is suspected (not just latency), page Runtime Kernels and Runtime Architecture/perf guardrails immediately.

---

## Changelog (recent)
- 2026-02-26: Added FP8 decode allowlist-only note (KASV2-005) and clarified customer guidance.
- 2026-02-25: Updated L40S + driver 535.x crash details; elevated to hard denylist (KASV2-002).
- 2026-02-21: Added long-context tail regression watchlist and preferred mitigations (KASV2-001).
- 2026-02-14: Documented telemetry cardinality mitigation (KASV2-006).

title: Perf suite: expand coverage for long-context + mixed workloads; define pass/fail thresholds (kernel selector v2)
text:
description:
Context
Kernel auto-selection v2 is being rolled out behind gates. Current perf suite coverage under-represents long-context prompts (large prefill) and mixed prompt distributions that stress selector stability + batching/scheduling interactions. We also need explicit pass/fail thresholds for canary/GA decisions so we don’t debate “is this regression acceptable?” during rollout.

Goals
1) Expand benchmark coverage to include long-context and mixed workloads that match Dedicated/Private customer usage (summarization, RAG over long docs, batchy micro-prompts, and mixed prefill/decode ratios).
2) Define pass/fail thresholds for v2 vs v1 per (model family, seq-bucket regime, GPU SKU) and provide a single “canary gate” summary.
3) Ensure runs are reproducible/deterministic enough to catch tail-latency spikes (p95/p99) without flakiness.

Non-goals
- Not building a full eval/quality harness (handled by Perf & Evals separately).
- Not tuning selector thresholds here (that stays in selector PRs); this ticket only expands measurement + gating.

What to add (coverage)
A) Long-context scenarios (prefill-heavy)
- Context lengths: 8k, 16k, 32k tokens (where model supports), with decode lengths: 64, 256.
- Measure TTFT (time-to-first-token), prefill latency, and p95/p99 for first token + steady-state decode.
- Include at least one “near-memory-limit” prompt (but safe) to surface kernel choices that increase peak memory.

B) Mixed workloads (selector stability + scheduling interaction)
- Mix distributions within a single run (same worker pool):
  - 70/20/10 short/medium/long (e.g., 512/2k/16k prefill) with decode 128.
  - 50/50 interactive vs batchy (short requests with concurrency spikes vs medium requests with steady concurrency).
- Add “two-peak” distribution (most requests small, occasional very long) to replicate tail amplification.
- Ensure selector gets consistent features: model family tag, seq-bucket, GPU SKU; record selection decisions for correlation.

C) Model family coverage (minimum set for gating)
- Llama family (e.g., Llama-3 class)
- Mistral family
- Qwen family
- Gemma family
Note: the actual model IDs used in perf suite should follow the existing benchmark-lab naming + availability per GPU.

D) GPU SKUs (minimum set)
- A100 80GB
- H100 (SXM where available; PCIe acceptable if that’s what benchmark-lab has)
- L40S
- If available in lab: A100 40GB (or MIG slice) as “constrained memory” signal.

Metrics to record (must-have)
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for TTFT, end-to-end, and per-token decode (where supported).
- Throughput: tokens/sec (decode), requests/sec, and effective batch size distribution.
- Error/health: OOM rate, kernel launch failures, retried requests (if visible), and % fallback kernel usage.
- Selector telemetry correlation keys: selected_kernel, candidate_set_size, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_norm, model_family, selector_version, gate_state (v1/v2).

Pass/Fail thresholds (proposed for runtime-1.21 rollout)
Definitions
- Baseline is selector v1 on same commit (or closest stable) and same environment.
- Compare v2 vs v1 per (model family × scenario × GPU SKU). Use same seeds and at least N=5 repetitions; aggregate by median of runs for p95/p99 to reduce flake.

Hard fail (block canary expansion / trigger rollback recommendation)
- p99 end-to-end latency regression > +8% in any long-context scenario on any “supported” GPU SKU.
- p95 TTFT regression > +10% in long-context (16k/32k) scenarios.
- Error rate increase > +0.25% absolute (OOMs, launch failures) in any scenario.
- Fallback rate (to “safe” kernel) increases by > +15% absolute without corresponding error improvements (indicates mis-selection / denylist gaps).

Soft fail (requires sign-off from Runtime Architect + SRE before proceeding)
- p99 regression between +5% and +8% in any scenario.
- p95 regression between +3% and +5% in mixed workloads.
- Increased variance/run-to-run instability: coefficient of variation (CoV) for p99 > 0.12 across repetitions, unless explained by known noisy SKUs.

Success criteria (what we expect, not required to ship)
- Long-context: p95 TTFT improvement of 3–8% on H100 and A100 for 16k+ contexts (where selector chooses optimized prefill kernels).
- Mixed workloads: reduced p99 “spikes” relative to v1 due to better seq regime bucketing and fewer pathological kernel choices.

Implementation plan
1) Harness additions (benchmark-lab)
- Add new workload config format for “mixture distributions” (weighted scenario sets per run).
- Add prompt corpus entries for long-context (synthetic + a small set of real-ish docs). Ensure PII-free.
- Add seed pinning + run metadata capture (git SHA, driver/CUDA, selector gate state).

2) Scenario definitions (perf-canary)
- Add canary scenarios for v1 vs v2 comparisons for:
  - long-context 16k/32k
  - mixed short+long distribution
- Wire to alert thresholds using the hard fail rules above.

3) Reporting
- Produce a single summary table per commit: by GPU SKU and scenario with deltas vs baseline.
- Add an “explainability” section that links deltas to selector telemetry (e.g., kernel chosen frequency shifts).

4) Documentation
- Update the benchmark matrix Confluence page and include these new scenarios + thresholds.

Links / related artifacts
- Epic: sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-kernel-auto-selection-v2-epic.json
- Perf canary PR: sources/github/perf-canary/pr-1932-add-kernel-selection-v2-canary-scenarios.json
- Microbench PR (selector overhead): sources/github/benchmark-lab/pr-811-add-microbench-for-kernel-switch-overhead.json
- Working perf results sheet: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/kernel-autoselection-v2-perf-results.json
- Benchmark matrix doc: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/kernel-selection-v2-benchmark-matrix.json

Acceptance criteria
- Perf suite includes long-context scenarios (8k/16k/32k where available) and at least two mixed-workload distributions.
- Runs emit required selector correlation fields so regressions can be tied to selection decisions.
- Pass/fail thresholds are codified in perf-canary (automated) and documented in the benchmark matrix.
- Canary gate summary is stable (no chronic flakes) across at least 10 consecutive runs on each primary SKU.

Risks / gotchas
- Long-context runs are slow; need to balance coverage vs CI time. Plan: keep full matrix in nightly; keep minimal gating set in per-PR canary.
- Metric cardinality explosion if we tag too many fields. Work with Omar/Logan to ensure sampling + low-cardinality normalization (gpu_sku_norm, model_family enums).
- Lab hardware availability (H100) may delay full coverage; use staged enablement by SKU with clear “coverage gaps” called out in rollup.

Requested reviewers / stakeholders
- Claire Dubois (benchmark methodology)
- Jonas Weber (Perf & Evals)
- Lena Fischer (workload regime characterization)
- Omar El-Sayed (tail latency + observability constraints)
- Sahana Iyer (CI capacity + GPU runners)


comments:
2026-01-17 (Claire Dubois): Marking as P0 because long-context is the top risk area for selector v2 tail spikes. Please include at least one scenario where 1–2% of requests are very long (16k+) mixed into mostly short traffic; that’s the Dedicated customer pattern we keep seeing.
2026-01-22 (Marcus Reed): Started implementation in benchmark-lab: added mixture-distribution config support locally; will upstream once I confirm it doesn’t break existing single-scenario runners. Also pulling 20 sanitized long-doc prompts from the existing internal corpus (PII-free) + synthetic token fillers for exact lengths.
2026-02-01 (Sahana Iyer): Heads up CI GPU runner capacity is tight for H100 this week. Suggest we make H100 long-context 32k a nightly-only gate; keep 16k on PR canary.
2026-02-06 (Omar El-Sayed): For correlation fields, please use gpu_sku_norm and model_family only (no raw instance type) and keep selected_kernel as a bounded enum. We already saw a false-positive alert due to cardinality drift elsewhere; don’t repeat that here.
2026-02-11 (Marcus Reed): Proposed thresholds drafted in ticket description. Need sign-off from Noah + Aisha on the hard fail %s before wiring into perf-canary. Early data (A100): v2 improves p95 TTFT ~4% at 16k but regresses p99 ~6% on one mixed workload; suspect kernel choice oscillation when long requests arrive (selector hinting issue).
2026-02-18 (Lena Fischer): Mixed-workload definition looks good. Please ensure the runner can simulate bursts (e.g., 5x concurrency for 30s) because regime classification can be sensitive to observed distribution windows.
2026-02-24 (Marcus Reed): Implemented burst mode + two-peak distribution in a feature branch; waiting on review from Rina/Claire. Next: land minimal gate scenarios in perf-canary and move full matrix to nightly.
